classification.difficultyReason: The parts scaffold conversion of depression angles, a right-triangle length calculation and triangle angle calculations before combining those results with the sine rule.

content.prompt: An observation tower, $OT$, is 30 m high. From the top of the tower $T$, the angle of depression to the base $A$ of a small tree is $17^\circ$, while the angle of depression to the top of the tree, $B$, is $12^\circ$.

spec.description: Vertical tower OT and shorter vertical tree AB on horizontal OA; dashed horizontal reference and sightlines TB and TA. Separate depression-angle marks and a right-angle marker at O. Ordinary marks use house black; no fill.
spec.mathematics: OT=30 m; depression to B is 12 degrees and to A is 17 degrees; OT and AB are perpendicular to OA.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the value of $\angle OAT$, and hence find the length of $AT$, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
The horizontal through $T$ is parallel to $OA$, so alternate angles give $\angle OAT=17^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin17^\circ&=\frac{30}{AT}\\AT&=\frac{30}{\sin17^\circ}\\AT&\approx102.61\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the size of each of the angles in $\triangle ABT$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\angle ATB&=17^\circ-12^\circ\\\angle ATB&=5^\circ\\\angle BAT&=90^\circ-17^\circ\\\angle BAT&=73^\circ\\\angle ABT&=180^\circ-5^\circ-73^\circ\\\angle ABT&=102^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence, find the height of the tree, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Using the sine rule in $\triangle ABT$, with the unrounded value of $AT$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{\sin5^\circ}&=\frac{AT}{\sin102^\circ}\\AB&=\frac{30\sin5^\circ}{\sin17^\circ\sin102^\circ}\\AB&\approx9.14\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
